'''Abraham''' "'''Avi'''" '''Loeb''' ({{langx|he|אברהם (אבי) לייב}}; born February 26, 1962) is an Israeli-American [[Theoretical physics|theoretical physicist]] who works on [[astrophysics]] and [[cosmology]]. Loeb is the Frank B. Baird Jr. Professor of Science at [[Harvard University]].<ref name="BioITC">
{{cite web |title=Avi Loeb |url=https://itc.cfa.harvard.edu/people/avi-loeb |website=Institute for Theory and Computation @ Harvard University |publisher=Harvard University}}</ref><ref name="BioCFA">
{{cite web |title=Professor Avi Loeb |url=https://www.cfa.harvard.edu/~loeb |website=Harvard & Smithsonian Center For Astronomy |publisher=Harvard University}}</ref><ref name="BioBHI">
{{cite web |title=Abraham (Avi) Loeb |url=https://bhi.fas.harvard.edu/people/avi-loeb |website=Black Hole Initiative @ Harvard University |publisher=Harvard University}}</ref><ref name="Autobiography">
{{cite web |last1=Loeb |first1=Avi |title=Autobiographical sketch |url=https://www.cfa.harvard.edu/~loeb/Loeb_Autobiography.pdf |website=Harvard University}}</ref><ref name="CV">
{{cite web |last1=Loeb |first1=Abraham |title=Curriculum Vitae of Abraham Loeb |url=https://lweb.cfa.harvard.edu/~loeb/vitae.pdf |website=[[Harvard–Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics]]}}</ref><ref name="BioDepAstro">
{{cite web |title=Avi Loeb |url=https://astronomy.fas.harvard.edu/people/avi-loeb |website=Department of Astronomy @ Harvard University |publisher=Harvard University}}</ref> He chaired the Department of Astronomy from 2011 to 2020, and founded the [[Black Hole Initiative]] in 2016.

Loeb is a fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]], the [[American Physical Society]], and the [[International Academy of Astronautics]]. In 2015, he was appointed as the science theory director for the [[Breakthrough Initiatives]] of the [[Breakthrough Prize]] Foundation.

Loeb has published popular science books including ''[[Extraterrestrial: The First Sign of Intelligent Life Beyond Earth]]'' (2021) and ''Interstellar: The Search for Extraterrestrial Life and Our Future in the Stars'' (2023).

Since 2017, Loeb has made a series of pseudoscientific claims that alien space craft may be in the [[Solar System]]. He has argued that [[ʻOumuamua]] and other [[interstellar object]]s, including the reputedly interstellar [[meteor]] [[CNEOS 2014-01-08]], are potential examples of such craft.<ref name="CT-20190204">{{cite news |last=Groll |first=Johan |title=Thinking About Distant Civilizations Isn't Speculative |url=http://www.spiegel.de/international/zeitgeist/astronomer-avi-loeb-on-the-interstellar-body-oumuamua-a-1246803.html |date=January 7, 2019 |work=[[Der Spiegel]] |access-date=January 7, 2019 }}</ref> These claims have been widely rejected by the scientific community.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" /><ref name=":4">{{Cite web |date=2021-11-18 |title='Oumuamua wasn't an alien spacecraft, and ignoring the science can't make it so |url=https://bigthink.com/starts-with-a-bang/oumuamua-alien-spacecraft/ |access-date=2025-07-29 |website=Big Think |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2023, he claimed to have recovered spherules formed by the impact of CNEOS 2014-01-08 that he alleged could be evidence of an alien starship,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-07-05 |title=Why a Harvard professor thinks he may have found fragments of an alien spacecraft |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/avi-loeb-interstellar-object-aliens-b2369534.html |access-date=2023-07-25 |website=The Independent |language=en}}</ref> but the location in the ocean where he recovered the spherules was based on mistaking a seismic signal from a truck for the impact of the meteor.<ref name="NYT-20230724" /><ref name=":3" /> Loeb tends to publicize his results before undergoing [[peer review]], contributing to a climate of sensationalism around his claims.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Miller |first=Katrina |date=July 24, 2023 |title=Scientist's Deep Dive for Alien Life Leaves His Peers Dubious (Published 2023) |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/07/24/science/avi-loeb-extraterrestrial-life.html |access-date=2025-11-21 |work=[[The New York Times]] |language=en |quote=Many astronomers, though, see the announcement as the latest example of Dr. Loeb making an outlandish declaration that is too strong and too hasty. His pronouncements (and a promotional video in Times Square about the search for extraterrestrial life) skew public perception of how science actually works, they say. <br/> “People are sick of hearing about Avi Loeb’s wild claims,” said Steve Desch, an astrophysicist at Arizona State University. “It’s polluting good science — conflating the good science we do with this ridiculous sensationalism and sucking all the oxygen out of the room.”<br/> Dr. Desch added that several of his colleagues were now refusing to engage with Dr. Loeb’s work in peer review, the process by which scholars evaluate one another’s research to ensure that only high-quality studies are published. “It’s a real breakdown of the peer review process and the scientific method,” he said. “And it’s so demoralizing and tiring.”}}</ref>

==Life and career==
Loeb was born in [[Beit Hanan]],<ref>{{cite news |last1=Carmeli |first1=Oded |title=If true, this could be one of the greatest discoveries in human history |url=https://www.haaretz.com/us-news/2019-01-16/ty-article-magazine/.premium/if-true-this-could-be-one-of-the-greatest-discoveries-in-human-history/0000017f-e880-df5f-a17f-fbde98f70000 |work=Haaretz.com |date=2019 |language=en}}</ref> Israel, in 1962. He took part in the [[Talpiot program|Talpiot research program]] while serving in the [[Israel Defense Forces]] at age 18.<ref name=":5">[https://www.afhu.org/2018/10/24/avi-loeb/ Avi Loeb] - website [[American Friends of the Hebrew University]]</ref> While in Talpiot, he obtained a [[Bachelor of Science|BSc]] degree in physics and mathematics in 1983, an [[Master of Science|MSc]] degree in physics in 1985, and a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in plasma physics in 1986, all from the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]] (HUJI).<ref name="CV" /> During his doctoral studies, Loeb conducted research at the [[Soreq Nuclear Research Center]] in [[Yavne]].<ref name=":5" /> His PhD thesis focused on the modeling of [[plasma acceleration]] of [[charged particle]]s.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Loeb |first=Abraham |date=1986 |title=Particle acceleration to high energies and amplification of coherent radiation by electromagnetic interactions in plasmas |url=https://inis.iaea.org/records/3bc5b-b0b03}}</ref> From 1983 to 1988, he was invited by the [[Strategic Defense Initiative|U.S. Strategic Defense Initiative]] to work on a new [[propulsion method]] for high-speed projectiles.<ref name="wonder">{{Cite web |last=Gritz |first=Jennie Rothenberg |title=The Wonder of Avi Loeb |url=https://www.smithsonianmag.com/science-nature/wonder-avi-loeb-180978579/ |access-date=2025-10-23 |website=[[Smithsonian Magazine]] |language=en}}</ref> Between 1988 and 1993, Loeb was a long-term member at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] at Princeton, where he started to work in [[theoretical astrophysics]] under the supervision of [[John Bahcall]].

In 1993, he moved to [[Harvard University]] as an assistant professor in the department of [[astronomy]], and was [[tenure]]d three years later.<ref name="Autobiography" /><ref name="BioDepAstro" /><ref name="BioCFA" /> Since 2007, he has been Director of the Institute for Theory and Computation at the [[Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics]].<ref name="BioITC"/> Since 2012, Loeb became the Frank B. Baird Jr. Professor of Science at Harvard.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2012-09-10 |title=Avi Loeb appointed the Frank B. Baird Jr. Professor of Science {{!}} Department of Astronomy |url=https://astronomy.fas.harvard.edu/announcements/avi-loeb-appointed-frank-b-baird-jr-professor-science |website=astronomy.fas.harvard.edu |language=en}}</ref>

Loeb has written eight books, including the textbooks ''How Did the First Stars and Galaxies Form?''<ref>[http://cfa-www.harvard.edu/~loeb/Loeb_book.pdf "How Did the First Stars and Galaxies Form?" book jacket (pdf)]</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Loeb |first1=Abraham |url=http://press.princeton.edu/titles/9373.html |title=Loeb, A.: How Did the First Stars and Galaxies Form? (eBook and Paperback) |date=February 8, 2016 |publisher=Princeton University Press |isbn=978-0-691-14516-7 |access-date=February 19, 2016}}</ref> and ''The First Galaxies in the Universe''.<ref>{{cite web |title="The First Galaxies in the Universe" by Loeb and Furlanetto |url=https://www.cfa.harvard.edu/~loeb/LF/ |access-date=February 19, 2016 |website=Cfa.harvard.edu}}</ref> He has co-authored many papers on topics in astrophysics and cosmology,<ref name="BioCFA"/><ref name="CV"/> including the first stars, the epoch of [[reionization]], the formation and evolution of massive [[black holes]], the search for extraterrestrial life, [[gravitational lensing]] by planets, [[gamma-ray bursts]] at high [[redshift]]s, the use of the [[Lyman-alpha forest]] to measure the acceleration/deceleration of the universe in real time,<ref>{{cite journal|author=Abraham Loeb |title=Direct Measurement of Cosmological Parameters from the Cosmic Deceleration of Extragalactic Objects |journal=[[The Astrophysical Journal]] |volume=499 |issue=2 |pages=L111–L114 |date=1998 |arxiv = astro-ph/9802122 |bibcode = 1998ApJ...499L.111L |doi = 10.1086/311375 |s2cid=6479300 }}</ref> the future collision between the [[Milky Way]] and [[Andromeda Galaxy|Andromeda]] galaxies,<ref>{{cite journal | bibcode = 2008MNRAS.386..461C | title=The collision between the Milky Way and Andromeda | journal=[[Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society]] | volume=386 | issue=1 | pages=461–474 | year=2008 | doi=10.1111/j.1365-2966.2008.13048.x|arxiv = 0705.1170 | last1=Cox | first1=T. J. | last2=Loeb | first2=Abraham | doi-access=free | s2cid=14964036 }}</ref> the future state of extragalactic astronomy,<ref>{{cite journal | bibcode = 2002PhRvD..65d7301L | title=Long-term future of extragalactic astronomy | journal=[[Physical Review D]] | volume=65 | issue=4 | article-number=47301 | year=2002|arxiv = astro-ph/0107568 |doi = 10.1103/PhysRevD.65.047301 | last1=Loeb | first1=Abraham | s2cid=1791226 }}</ref> astrophysical implications of black hole recoil in galaxy mergers,<ref>{{cite journal | bibcode = 2012MNRAS.421.2737O | title=Recoiled star clusters in the Milky Way halo: N-body simulations and a candidate search through the SDSS | journal=[[Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society]] | volume=421 | issue=4 | pages=2737–2750 | year=2012 | doi=10.1111/j.1365-2966.2011.20078.x|arxiv = 1102.3695 | last1=o'Leary | first1=Ryan M. | last2=Loeb | first2=Abraham | doi-access=free | s2cid=118524459 }}</ref> tidal disruption of stars,<ref>{{cite journal | bibcode = 2012PhRvL.108f1302S | title=Observing Lense-Thirring Precession in Tidal Disruption Flares | journal=[[Physical Review Letters]] | volume=108 | issue=6 | article-number=61302 | year=2012|arxiv = 1109.6660 |doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.108.061302 | pmid=22401052 | last1 = Stone | first1 = N | last2 = Loeb | first2 = A| s2cid=33103563 }}</ref> and imaging black hole silhouettes.<ref>{{cite journal | bibcode = 2006JPhCS..54..448B | title=Testing General Relativity with High-Resolution Imaging of Sgr A* | journal=[[Journal of Physics: Conference Series]] | volume=54 | pages=448–455 | year=2006 | doi=10.1088/1742-6596/54/1/070|arxiv = astro-ph/0607279 | last1=Broderick | first1=Avery E. | last2=Loeb | first2=Abraham | s2cid=16053017 }}</ref><ref name=BioBHI/>

Together with his [[Postdoctoral researcher|postdoc]] James Guillochon, Loeb predicted the existence of a new population of stars moving near the speed of light throughout the universe.<ref>{{cite news|last=Lemonick|first=Michael D.|date=November 26, 2014|title=You've Heard of Shooting Stars, But This is Ridiculous|magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]]|url=https://time.com/3602047/hypervelocity-stars/}}</ref> Together with his postdoc John Forbes and Howard Chen of [[Northwestern University]], Loeb made another prediction that sub-Neptune-sized exoplanets have been transformed into rocky [[super-Earths]] by the activity of the black hole [[Sagittarius A*]].<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Howard Chen|author2=John C. Forbes|author3=Abraham Loeb|date=2018|title=Habitable Evaporated Cores and the Occurrence of Panspermia Near the Galactic Center|journal=[[The Astrophysical Journal Letters]]|volume=855|issue=1|pages=L1|arxiv=1711.06692|bibcode=2018ApJ...855L...1C|doi=10.3847/2041-8213/aaab46|s2cid=119398803 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

Together with Paolo Pani, Loeb showed in 2013 that primordial black holes in the range between the masses of the Moon and the Sun cannot make up [[dark matter]].<ref>{{cite news| url=https://science.time.com/2013/09/05/the-mystery-of-dark-matter-clarified-a-little/ | magazine=Time | title=The Mystery of Dark Matter Clarified—a Little | date=September 5, 2013}}</ref> In 2025, Loeb, in collaboration with Oem Trivedi, proposed that dark matter could consist of remnants of [[Planck star|Planck Stars]] formed after the evaporation of primordial black holes.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Trivedi |first1=Oem |last2=Loeb |first2=Avi |title=Could Planck Star Remnants Be Dark Matter? |journal=Physics of the Dark Universe |volume=44 |year=2025 |article-number=102003 |doi=10.1016/j.dark.2025.102003 |arxiv=2506.03334 |bibcode=2025PDU....4902003T }}</ref> Loeb led a team that reported tentative evidence for the birth of a black hole in the young nearby supernova [[SN 1979C]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.npr.org/2010/11/15/131336737/supernova-shines-light-on-black-hole-formation?ft=1&f=1026 |title=Supernova Shines Light On Black Hole Formation |website=NPR.org |access-date=February 19, 2016}}</ref> In collaboration with Dan Maoz, Loeb demonstrated in 2013 that [[biomarker]]s, such as molecular oxygen ({{chem|O|2}}), can be detected by the [[James Webb Space Telescope]] (JWST) in the atmosphere of Earth-mass planets in the [[habitable zone]] of [[white dwarf]]s.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://science.time.com/2013/03/06/could-tiny-stars-be-home-to-mirror-earths/ | magazine=Time | title=Could Tiny Stars Be Home to Mirror Earths? | date=March 6, 2013}}</ref>

In 2018, he served a term as chair of the board on Physics and Astronomy (BPA)<ref>{{cite web |title=BPA |url=http://sites.nationalacademies.org/BPA/index.htm |access-date=September 7, 2016 |website=nationalacademies.org}}</ref> of the [[National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine]] (NASEM).

===Life in the universe===
In 2013, Loeb wrote about the "Habitable Epoch of the Early Universe", noting that the [[Cosmic microwave background|Cosmic Microwave Background]] would temporarily have been at temperatures compatible with liquid water around 15 million years after the [[Big Bang]].<ref name="ARXIV-20131202">{{cite journal|last1=Loeb|first1=Abraham|title=The habitable epoch of the early Universe|journal=[[International Journal of Astrobiology]]|date=September 9, 2014|volume=13|issue=4|pages=337–339|doi=10.1017/S1473550414000196|arxiv = 1312.0613 |bibcode = 2014IJAsB..13..337L |s2cid=2777386}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|author=Adam Frank |url=https://www.npr.org/blogs/13.7/2014/02/03/271093289/eureka-first-life-in-the-universe |title=First Life In The Universe: 13.7: Cosmos And Culture |website=NPR.org |date=February 4, 2014 |access-date=February 19, 2016}}</ref> In April 2021, he presented an updated summary of his ideas of life in the early universe.<ref name="SA-20210404">{{cite news |last=Loeb |first=Avi |title=When Did Life First Emerge in the Universe? - We don't know, but we could try to find out by searching for it on planets orbiting the very oldest stars |url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/when-did-life-first-emerge-in-the-universe/ |date=April 4, 2021 |work=[[Scientific American]] |access-date=April 4, 2021 }}</ref>

In 2020, Loeb published a paper about the possibility that life can propagate from one planet to another,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Siraj|first1=Amir|last2=Loeb|first2=Abraham|date=April 17, 2020|title=Possible Transfer of Life by Earth-Grazing Objects to Exoplanetary Systems|journal=Life|volume=10|issue=4|page=44|doi=10.3390/life10040044|issn=2075-1729|pmc=7235815|pmid=32316564|arxiv=2001.02235|bibcode=2020Life...10...44S |doi-access=free}}</ref> followed by the opinion piece "Noah's Spaceship" about [[directed panspermia]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Loeb|first=Avi|date=November 29, 2020|title=Noah's Spaceship|url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/noahs-spaceship/|url-status=live|access-date=February 18, 2021|website=Scientific American|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201129170232/https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/noahs-spaceship/ |archive-date=November 29, 2020 }}</ref>

=== Claims about alien life ===
Loeb's claims about [[Extraterrestrial life|alien life]] have attracted sustained criticism from other scientists. Steve Desch, an astrophysicist at [[Arizona State University]] referred to Loeb's claims as "ridiculous sensationalism" which represent "a real breakdown of the peer review process and the scientific method".<ref name="NYT-20230724" /> Some of Loeb's claims have been described as conspiracy theories, with ''[[USA Today]]'' referring to Loeb's speculation about 3I/ATLAS as an "outlandish conspiracy theor[y]."<ref name=":7">{{Cite web |last=Lagatta |first=Eric |title=NASA drops never-before-seen photos of interstellar 3I/ATLAS. Here's a look |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/2025/11/20/3iatlas-photos-nasa-images-alien/87350869007/ |access-date=2025-11-21 |website=USA TODAY |language=en-US |quote=The strange outsider's jaunt through Earth's cosmic neighborhood has sparked plenty of outlandish conspiracy theories regarding its nature.<br/>One particularly infamous idea – put forth by a Harvard astrophysicist named Avi Loeb – is that 3I/ATLAS could be an alien spaceship. Though Loeb has conceded on publishing platform Medium that the object is "most likely a comet of natural origin," he has not ruled out the possibility that it could be extraterrestrial technology.|date=20 November 2025}}</ref> Other scientists have described Loeb's theories as "nonsense", comparable to the idea that "the moon is made of cheese."<ref name=":6">{{Cite news |last=Dunham |first=Will |title=NASA releases images of comet 3I/ATLAS, rejects alien spacecraft 'rumors' |url=https://www.reuters.com/science/nasa-set-release-new-images-interstellar-object-3iatlas-2025-11-19/ |work=[[Reuters]] |quote=University of Oxford astrophysicist Chris Lintott told Reuters: "So far, it seems to be made of the same sort of stuff we see for comets in our solar system - plenty of carbon dioxide and some water, carbon monoxide and other such molecules. We've also seen cyanide - normal for a comet - and lots of nickel, which is a bit surprising but not too unprecedented. We saw similar things in a previous interstellar comet, 2I/Borisov, and in some solar system comets."<br/>"The idea that 3I/ATLAS could be an alien spacecraft is simply nonsense. There's nothing about it that suggests such a thing, and you might as well argue that the moon is made of cheese," Lintott said.|date=19 November 2025}}</ref>

==== ʻOumuamua ====
{{main|ʻOumuamua}}
[[1I/ʻOumuamua|ʻOumuamua]] was the first confirmed interstellar object detected in the [[Solar System]]. In December 2017, Loeb cited ʻOumuamua's unusually elongated shape as one of the reasons the [[Green Bank Telescope]] in West Virginia should listen for [[radio emission]]s from it to see if there were any unexpected signs that it might be of [[Extraterrestrial intelligence|artificial origin]],<ref name=Guarddian2017-12-11>{{Cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/2017/dec/11/astronomers-to-check-interstellar-body-for-signs-of-alien-technology |title=Astronomers to check interstellar body for signs of alien technology |author=Ian Sample |journal=The Guardian |date=December 11, 2017 |quote=Green Bank telescope in West Virginia will listen for radio signals from ʻOumuamua, an object from another solar system ... "Most likely it is of natural origin, but because it is so peculiar, we would like to check if it has any sign of artificial origin, such as radio emissions," said Avi Loeb, professor of astronomy at Harvard University and an adviser to the Breakthrough Listen project. "If we do detect a signal that appears artificial in origin, we'll know immediately." ... While many astronomers believe the object is an interstellar asteroid, its elongated shape is unlike anything seen in the asteroid belt in our own solar system. Early observations of ʻOumuamua show that it is about 400m long but only one tenth as wide. "It's curious that the first object we see from outside the solar system looks like that," said Loeb. |access-date=December 12, 2017}}</ref> although earlier limited observations by other radio telescopes such as the [[SETI Institute]]'s [[Allen Telescope Array]] had produced no such results.<ref name=SETI>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/alien-probe-or-galactic-driftwood-seti-tunes-in-to-oumuamua/ |title=Alien Probe or Galactic Driftwood? SETI Tunes In to ʻOumuamua |magazine=[[Scientific American]] |first=Lee |last=Billings |date=December 11, 2017 |access-date=December 12, 2017 |quote=So far limited observations of 'Oumuamua, using facilities such as the SETI Institute's Allen Telescope Array, have turned up nothing.}}</ref> The Green Bank Telescope observed the asteroid for six hours, detecting no radio signals.<ref>{{cite web |title=Breakthrough Listen Releases Initial Results and Data from Observations of 'Oumuamua<!--Deny Citation Bot--> |url=http://breakthroughinitiatives.org/news/15 |publisher=Breakthrough Listen |date=December 13, 2017 |access-date=December 15, 2017 |quote="No evidence of artificial signals emanating from the object so far detected by the Green Bank Telescope, but monitoring and analysis continue. Initial data are available for public inspection in the Breakthrough Listen archive"}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/2017/dec/14/is-oumuamua-an-alien-spacecraft-first-scans-show-no-signs-of-technology |title=Is 'Oumuamua an alien spacecraft? Initial scans show no signs of technology<!--Deny Citation Bot--> |journal=The Guardian |author=Ian Sample |date=December 15, 2017 |access-date=December 15, 2017}}</ref>

On October 26, 2018, Loeb and his postdoctoral student Shmuel Bialy submitted a paper exploring the possibility that ʻOumuamua is an artificial thin [[solar sail]] accelerated by solar radiation pressure in an effort to help explain the object's non-gravitational acceleration.<ref name="UT-230181031">{{cite web |last=Williams |first=Matt |title=Could Oumuamua Be an Extra-Terrestrial Solar Sail? |url=https://www.universetoday.com/140391/could-oumuamua-be-an-extra-terrestrial-solar-sail/ |date=November 2, 2018 |work=[[Universe Today]] |access-date=November 2, 2018 }}</ref><ref name="ARX-20181101">{{cite journal |last1=Bialy |first1=Shmuel |last2=Loeb |first2=Abraham |s2cid=118956077 |title= Could Solar Radiation Pressure Explain 'Oumuamua's Peculiar Acceleration?|journal=The Astrophysical Journal |date=October 26, 2018 |volume=868 |issue=1 |pages=L1 |arxiv=1810.11490|doi=10.3847/2041-8213/aaeda8 |bibcode=2018ApJ...868L...1B |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name="SA-201809287">{{cite web |last=Loeb |first=Abraham |title=How to Search for Dead Cosmic Civilizations |url=https://blogs.scientificamerican.com/observations/how-to-search-for-dead-cosmic-civilizations/ |date=September 26, 2018 |work=[[Scientific American]] |access-date=September 26, 2018 }}</ref> The consensus among other astrophysicists was that the available evidence is insufficient to consider such a premise,<ref>[https://phys.org/news/2018-11-scientists-harvard-alien-spacecraft-theory.html Scientists push back against Harvard 'alien spacecraft' theory]. Kerry Sheridan, PhysOrg. November 7, 2018.</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.yahoo.com/news/oumuamua-oh-interstellar-object-actually-225825249.html|title='Oumuamua, oh my! Was interstellar object actually an alien solar sail? Not so fast|last=Boyle|first=Alan|date=November 6, 2018|website=Yahoo!|access-date=November 8, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.zeit.de/wissen/2018-11/oumuamua-lichtsegel-ausserirdische-aliens|title=Glaubt dieser Harvard-Professor selbst, was er sagt?|last=Schadwinkel|first=Alina|date=November 8, 2018|work=Zeit Online|access-date=November 8, 2018}}</ref> and that a tumbling solar sail would not be able to accelerate.<ref>[https://www.wpsdlocal6.com/2018/11/06/cigar-shaped-interstellar-object-may-have-been-an-alien-probe-harvard-paper-claims/ Cigar-shaped interstellar object may have been an alien probe, Harvard paper claims]. CNN News. November 6, 2018.</ref><ref name="TA-20190123">{{cite web |last=Koren |first=Marina |title=When a Harvard Professor Talks About Aliens – News about extraterrestrial life sounds better coming from an expert at a high-prestige institution. |url=https://www.theatlantic.com/science/archive/2019/01/oumuamua-interstellar-harvard-astrophysicist/580948/ |date=January 23, 2019 |work=[[The Atlantic]] |access-date=January 23, 2019 }}</ref> In response, Loeb wrote an article detailing six anomalous properties of ʻOumuamua that make it unusual, unlike any comets or asteroids seen before.<ref name="SA-20181120">{{cite web |last=Loeb |first=Abraham |author-link=Avi Loeb |title=6 Strange Facts about the Interstellar Visitor 'Oumuamua |url=https://blogs.scientificamerican.com/observations/6-strange-facts-about-the-interstellar-visitor-oumuamua/ |date=November 20, 2018 |work=[[Scientific American]] |access-date=November 20, 2018 }}</ref><ref name="TNY-20190116">{{cite magazine |last=Chotiner |first=Isaac |title=Have Aliens Found Us? A Harvard Astronomer on the Mysterious Interstellar Object 'Oumuamua |url=https://www.newyorker.com/news/the-new-yorker-interview/have-aliens-found-us-a-harvard-astronomer-on-the-mysterious-interstellar-object-oumuamua |date=January 16, 2019 |magazine=[[The New Yorker]] |access-date=January 16, 2019 }}</ref> By 2021, there was widespread consensus in the scientific community that 1I/ʻOumuamua had properties entirely consistent with a naturally occurring object, perhaps made of [[Solid nitrogen|nitrogen ice]],<ref name=":4" /> or a comet-like body that was altered by warming as it travelled through the solar system.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bergner |first1=Jennifer B. |last2=Seligman |first2=Darryl Z. |date=2023-03-23 |title=Acceleration of 1I/'Oumuamua from radiolytically produced H2 in H2O ice |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-022-05687-w |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=615 |issue=7953 |pages=610–613 |doi=10.1038/s41586-022-05687-w |pmid=36949336 |issn=0028-0836|arxiv=2303.13698 }}</ref>

On November 27, 2018, Loeb and [[Amir Siraj]], a Harvard undergraduate, proposed a search for ʻOumuamua-like objects that might be trapped in the Solar System as a result of losing orbital energy through a close encounter with [[Jupiter]].<ref name="ARX-20181109632">{{cite arXiv |last1=Siraj |first1=Amir |last2=Loeb |first2=Abraham |title=Identifying Interstellar Objects Trapped in the Solar System through Their Orbital Parameters |date=November 27, 2018 |eprint=1811.09632v2|class=astro-ph.EP }}</ref> They identified four candidates ([[2011 SP25]], [[2017 RR2]], [[2017 SV13]], and [[2018 TL6]]) for trapped interstellar objects that dedicated missions could visit. The authors pointed out that future sky surveys, such as with [[Large Synoptic Survey Telescope]], could find many more.<ref name="MNRAS-20181129">{{cite journal|last1=Siraj|first1=Amir|last2=Loeb|first2=Abraham|year=2019|title=Identifying Interstellar Objects Trapped in the Solar System through Their Orbital Parameters|journal=The Astrophysical Journal|volume=872|issue=1|pages=L10|arxiv=1811.09632|bibcode=2019ApJ...872L..10S|doi=10.3847/2041-8213/ab042a|s2cid=119198820 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

In public interviews and private communications with reporters and academic colleagues, Loeb has become more vocal about the prospects of proving the existence of alien life.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.nola.com/education/2019/02/harvards-top-astronomer-says-an-alien-ship-may-be-among-us.html|title=Harvard's top astronomer says an alien ship may be among us|last=Post|first=The Washington|website=nola.com|language=en-US|access-date=February 5, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190205154635/https://www.nola.com/education/2019/02/harvards-top-astronomer-says-an-alien-ship-may-be-among-us.html|archive-date=February 5, 2019}}</ref> On April 16, 2019, Loeb and Siraj reported the discovery of a meteor of interstellar origin.<ref name="Meteor">{{cite arXiv |author=Siraj, A. |author2=Loeb, A. |title= Discovery of a Meteor of Interstellar Origin |date=April 16, 2019 |class=astro-ph.EP |eprint=1904.07224 }}</ref> ''[[Extraterrestrial: The First Sign of Intelligent Life Beyond Earth]]'', a [[popular science]] account of ʻOumuamua by Loeb,<ref name="SA-20210622">{{cite news |last=Loeb |first=Avi |author-link=Avi Loeb |title=A Possible Link between 'Oumuamua and Unidentified Aerial Phenomena - If some UAP turn out to be extraterrestrial technology, they could be dropping sensors for a subsequent craft to tune into. What if 'Oumuamua is such a craft? |url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/a-possible-link-between-oumuamua-and-unidentified-aerial-phenomena/ |date=June 22, 2021 |work=[[Scientific American]] |access-date=June 22, 2021 }}</ref> was published in 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Object that whizzed by Earth probably came from alien world, Harvard professor asserts|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/alien-extraterrestrial-oumuamua-space-object-whizzed-by-earth-harvard-professor/|access-date=January 13, 2021|website=cbsnews.com|date=January 8, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Tucker|first=Reed|date=January 2, 2021|title=A Harvard professor says an alien visited in 2017 — and more are coming|url=https://nypost.com/2021/01/02/a-harvard-professor-says-an-alien-visited-in-2017/|access-date=January 13, 2021|website=New York Post|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Anderson|first=Travis|date=January 4, 2021|title=In new book, Harvard astronomer pushes theory about object that passed through solar system; alien world may have sent it – The Boston Globe|url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/2021/01/04/metro/new-book-harvard-astronomer-pushes-theory-about-object-that-passed-through-solar-system-alien-world-may-have-sent-it/|access-date=January 13, 2021|website=BostonGlobe.com|language=en-US}}</ref>

==== The Galileo Project ====
[[File:First all-sky Galileo Observatory for UAP on the roof of the Harvard College Observatory (Cambridge, MA).png|thumb|350px|"Constructing new telescope systems to infer the nature of Unidentified Aerial Phenomena (UAP), similar to those mentioned in the [[UFO Report (U.S. Intelligence)|ODNI report (ODNI 2021)]] to the US Congress"<ref name="2209.02479">{{Cite journal|last1=Loeb |first1=Abraham |title=Overview of the Galileo Project |journal=Journal of Astronomical Instrumentation |date=2023|volume=12 |issue=1 |article-number=2340003 |doi=10.1142/S2251171723400032 |arxiv=2209.02479 |bibcode=2023JAI....1240003L |s2cid=252089170 }}</ref>]]
{{Main|The Galileo Project}}

In July 2021, Loeb founded the Galileo Project for the Systematic Scientific Search for Evidence of Extraterrestrial Technological Artifacts.<ref name="galileo">{{cite web |title=The Galileo Project: "Daring to Look Through New Telescopes" |url=https://projects.iq.harvard.edu/galileo |publisher=Harvard University |access-date=August 12, 2021}}</ref><ref name="SA-20210919">{{cite news |last=Loeb |first=Avi |author-link=Avi Loeb |title=Astronomers Should be Willing to Look Closer at Weird Objects in the Sky - The Galileo Project seeks to train telescopes on unidentified aerial phenomena |url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/astronomers-should-be-willing-to-look-closer-at-weird-objects-in-the-sky/ |date=September 19, 2021 |work=[[Scientific American]] |access-date=September 19, 2021 }}</ref> The project was inspired by the detection of ʻOumuamua and by release of the Office of the Director of [[National Intelligence]] report on [[Unidentified Aerial Phenomena]] (UAP). As stated on the project's website, the aim is:

{{Cquote
| quote = Given the recently discovered abundance of Earth-Sun systems, the Galileo Project is dedicated to the proposition that humans can no longer ignore the possible existence of Extraterrestrial Technological Civilizations (ETCs), and that science should not dogmatically reject potential extraterrestrial explanations because of social stigma or cultural preferences, factors which are not conducive to the scientific method of unbiased, empirical inquiry. We now must 'dare to look through new telescopes', both literally and figuratively.<ref name="galileo"/>
}}

The three main avenues of research are:<ref>{{cite web |title=The Galileo Project: Activities |url=https://projects.iq.harvard.edu/galileo/activities |publisher=Harvard University}}</ref>
* Obtaining high-resolution images of UAPs and discovering their nature
* Searching for and research of ʻOumuamua-like interstellar objects
* Searching for potential ETC satellites

Unlike other similar projects, such as [[SETI]], the goal of the Galileo Project is to search for physical objects, and not electromagnetic signals, associated with extraterrestrial technological equipment.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Galileo Project |url=https://projects.iq.harvard.edu/galileo/home |access-date=2022-11-17 |website=projects.iq.harvard.edu |language=en}}</ref> The project was covered by many independent publishers, among them ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'', ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]'', ''[[The New York Post]]'', ''[[Scientific American]]'', ''[[The Guardian]]'', etc.<ref>{{cite web |title=The Galileo Project: Press Coverage |url=https://projects.iq.harvard.edu/galileo/press-coverage |publisher=Harvard University}}</ref> To allegations that [[Ufology|studies of UFOs]] is pseudoscience, Loeb answers that the project aims not to study UFOs based on previous data, but to study Unidentified Aerial Phenomena "using the standard scientific method based on a transparent analysis of open scientific data to be collected using optimized instruments".<ref>{{cite web |title=The Galileo Project: Scope |url=https://projects.iq.harvard.edu/galileo/scope |publisher=Harvard University |access-date=August 12, 2021}}</ref>

=====CNEOS 2014-01-08=====
{{main|CNEOS 2014-01-08}}

In 2014, the [[United States Department of Defense|US Department of Defense]] observed a fireball entering the atmosphere.<ref name="conversation spherules" /> Loeb made a series of claims about this event, from the meteor being from outside the Solar System to its likely area of impact based on, among other things, a seismic signal that occurred around the same time,<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=2024-03-13 |title=The humiliating truth behind Harvard astronomer's "alien" spherules |url=https://bigthink.com/starts-with-a-bang/truth-harvard-astronomer-alien-spherules/ |access-date=2024-07-15 |website=Big Think |language=en-US}}</ref> all culminating in 2023, when Loeb announced that he had found [[Interstellar object|interstellar material]] on the ocean floor<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2023-07-05 |title=I'm a Harvard astronomer. I think we found interstellar material |url=https://www.newsweek.com/harvard-astronomer-alien-discovery-interstellar-material-1811087 |access-date=2023-07-25 |website=Newsweek |language=en}}</ref> that he asserted came from the meteor and could be remnants of an [[Extraterrestrial life|extraterrestrial]] [[starship]].<ref name="conversation spherules">{{Cite web |last=Grady |first=Monica |date=2023-07-07 |title=Physicist who found spherical meteor fragments claims they may come from an alien spaceship – here's what to make of it |url=http://theconversation.com/physicist-who-found-spherical-meteor-fragments-claims-they-may-come-from-an-alien-spaceship-heres-what-to-make-of-it-209101 |access-date=2023-07-25 |website=The Conversation |language=en}}</ref> These claims were criticized by other scientists as hasty, sensational, and part of a pattern of improper behavior. Peter Brown, a meteor physicist at the [[University of Western Ontario]], argued the material can be explained as non-interstellar, noting that measurements from [[United States Department of Defense|Defense Department]] data are opaque and error-prone. Brown further said he was disturbed by Loeb's lack of engagement with relevant experts.<ref name="NYT-20230724">{{cite news |last=Miller |first=Katrina |title=Scientist's Deep Dive for Alien Life Leaves His Peers Dubious - Avi Loeb, a Harvard astrophysicist, says that material recovered from the seafloor could be from an extraterrestrial spacecraft. His peers are skeptical. + comment |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/07/24/science/avi-loeb-extraterrestrial-life.html |date=24 July 2023 |work=[[The New York Times]] |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230725025701/https://www.nytimes.com/2023/07/24/science/avi-loeb-extraterrestrial-life.html#permid=126537672 |archive-date=July 25, 2023 |access-date=24 July 2023 }}</ref> In March 2022, the [[United States Space Force|U.S. Space Force]] affirmed that their 2014 data indicated an interstellar origin, while the following month [[NASA]] stated the evidence for this was inconclusive.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |date=2022-04-15 |title=Harvard astronomer believes an interstellar meteor (or craft) smashed into Earth in 2014 — others aren't so sure |url=https://www.inverse.com/science/interstellar-meteor-2014-discovery |access-date=2023-11-17 |website=Inverse |language=en}}</ref>

Astrophysicist Steve Desch, at [[Arizona State University]], commented "[Loeb's claims are] polluting good science—conflating the good science we do with this ridiculous sensationalism and sucking all the oxygen out of the room", and said several of his colleagues are consequently refusing to engage with Loeb in the [[peer review]] process.<ref name="NYT-20230724" /> [[Monica Grady]] from the [[Open University]] argued that the evidence for Loeb's claims is "rather shaky" and pointed more plausibly to terrestrial pollution.<ref name="conversation spherules" /> Patricio A. Gallardo in an [[American Astronomical Society]] paper similarly concluded the samples were consistent with coal ash contamination.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Gallardo |first=Patricio A. |date=2023-10-19 |title=Anthropogenic Coal Ash as a Contaminant in a Micro-meteoritic Underwater Search |journal=Research Notes of the AAS |volume=7 |issue=10 |page=220 |doi=10.3847/2515-5172/ad03f9 |issn=2515-5172 |doi-access=free |bibcode=2023RNAAS...7..220G }}</ref> Loeb subsequently authored a preprint saying chemical analysis ruled out coal ash contamination and indicated extrasolar origins.<ref>{{Cite arXiv |last=Loeb |first=Abraham |display-authors=et al. |date=2024-02-15 |title=Chemical Classification of Spherules from the Pacific Ocean Site of the CNEOS 2014 January 8 (IM1) Bolide |eprint=2401.09882 |class=astro-ph.EP}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Loeb |first=Abraham |display-authors=et al.  |date=2024-01-19 |title=Recovery and Classification of Spherules from the Pacific Ocean Site of the CNEOS 2014 January 8 (IM1) Bolide |journal=Research Notes of the AAS |volume=8 |issue=10 |page=39 |doi=10.3847/2515-5172/ad2370 |issn=2515-5172 |doi-access=free |arxiv=2401.09882 |bibcode=2024RNAAS...8...39L }}</ref> Loeb and Morgan MacLeod proposed a tidal disruption mechanism that could cause meteors to be ejected into trajectories leading to the described observations.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Loeb |first=Abraham and MacLeod Morgan |date=2024-02-20 |title=Interstellar meteors from the tidal disruption of rocky planets on eccentric orbits around M dwarfs  |journal=Astronomy and Astrophysics |volume=686 |pages=A123 |doi=10.1051/0004-6361/202449250  |doi-access=free|arxiv=2310.09399 |bibcode=2024A&A...686A.123L }}</ref> In 2024 planetary seismologist Benjamin Fernando led a team that analyzed the seismic signals that led Loeb to search that specific region of the ocean, and they concluded that the seismic signals from one of the sensors used was in fact caused not by a meteor, but by a truck driving near the sensor, so that, "Not only did they use the wrong signal, they were looking in the wrong place."<ref name="Truck">{{cite web |last1=Krajick |first1=Kevin |title=Was It an Alien Spacecraft—Or a Delivery Truck? |url=https://news.climate.columbia.edu/2024/04/09/was-it-an-alien-spacecraft-or-a-delivery-truck/ |website=News from the Columbia Climate School |date=April 9, 2024 |publisher=Columbia |access-date=26 December 2024 |ref=ColumbiaAviLoeb}}</ref>

====3I/ATLAS====
{{main|3I/ATLAS#Alien spacecraft speculation}}

In 2025, ATLAS (Asteroid Terrestrial-impact Last Alert System), the NASA-funded survey telescope in [[Río Hurtado|Rio Hurtado]], Chile, observed a comet approaching from the constellation of [[Sagittarius (constellation)|Sagittarius]] at an interstellar velocity. Loeb hypothesized in the press that this, the third known interstellar object, could be an alien device with potentially malevolent intent. He based these speculations on his calculations of the likelihood of a comet of natural origins having these characteristics. "The retrograde orbital plane of 3I/ATLAS around the Sun lies within 5 degrees of that of Earth... The likelihood for that coincidence out of all random orientations is 0.2 percent," Loeb told ''Newsweek''. He further claimed that the brightness of 3I/ATLAS implies an object that is around 20 kilometers in diameter which is "too large for an interstellar asteroid." 3I/ATLAS' trajectory will bring it close to Venus, Mars and Jupiter, a path Loeb calculated as having a probability of just 0.005 percent. "It might have targeted the inner Solar System as expected from alien technology," he added. Richard Moissl, Head of Planetary Defence at the [[European Space Agency]] told Newsweek: "There have been no signs pointing to non-natural origins of 3I/ATLAS in the available observations."<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-07-21 |title=Harvard physicist claims new interstellar comet is alien probe |url=https://www.newsweek.com/interstellar-comet-alien-probe-harvard-physicist-avi-loeb-2101654 |access-date=2025-08-12 |website=Newsweek |language=en}}</ref> Since then, observations have reported evidence of 3I/ATLAS containing water, which is a substance commonly found in comets.<ref name="Yang2025">{{cite journal
  |first1 = Bin |last1 = Yang
  |first2 = Karen J. |last2 = Meech
  |first3 = Michael |last3 = Connelley
  |first4 = Jacqueline V. |last4 = Keane
  |title      = Spectroscopic Characterization of Interstellar Object 3I/ATLAS: Water Ice in the Coma
  |journal = The Astrophysical Journal
 |date       = 20 July 2025
  |volume = 992
 |issue = 1
 |pages = L9
 |doi = 10.3847/2041-8213/ae08a7
 |doi-access = free
 |arxiv     = 2507.14916
 |bibcode = 2025ApJ...992L...9Y
 }}</ref><ref name="Hopkins2025">{{cite journal
  |first1 = Matthew J. |last1 = Hopkins
  |first2 = Rosemary C. |last2 = Dorsey
  |first3 = John C. |last3 = Forbes
  |first4 = Michele T. |last4 = Bannister |author-link4 = Michele Bannister
  |first5 = Chris J. |last5 = Lintott |author-link5 = Chris Lintott
  |first6 = Brayden |last6 = Leicester
  |title      = From a Different Star: 3I/ATLAS in the Context of the Ōtautahi–Oxford Interstellar Object Population Model
  |journal = The Astrophysical Journal Letters
 |date       = 9 July 2025
  |volume = 990
 |issue = 2
 |pages = L30
 |doi = 10.3847/2041-8213/adfbf4
 |doi-access = free
 |arxiv     = 2507.05318
 |bibcode = 2025ApJ...990L..30H
 }}, Preprint, submitted to ApJ Letters</ref>

Independent assessments have resoundingly rejected the idea that 3I/ATLAS is anything except a comet. [[Nicola Fox]], associate administrator of NASA's [[Science Mission Directorate]] said that "We certainly haven't seen any technosignatures or anything from it that would lead us to believe it was anything other than a comet". Similarly, NASA Associate Administrator [[Amit Kshatriya]] stated that "all evidence points to it being a comet."<ref name=":6" /> In the face of this growing body of evidence, Loeb conceded that 3I/ATLAS is "most likely" a comet, though he continued to speculate about its supposed technological nature regardless.<ref name=":7" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Loeb |first=Abraham |author-link=Avi Loeb |date=29 Oct 2025 |title=A Q & A on 3I/ATLAS at Perihelion |url=https://avi-loeb.medium.com/a-q-a-on-3i-atlas-at-perihelion-62b7d592519b |website=Medium}}</ref>

===Relationship with mainstream science since 2017===
Since 2017,<ref name="wonder"/><ref>{{cite news |last1=Schelier |first1=Curt |title=Ignore it at your peril |url=https://jewishstandard.timesofisrael.com/ignore-it-at-your-peril/ |access-date=June 16, 2026 |work=[[Jewish Standard]] |date=September 28, 2023|quote=The starting point of the controversy occurred on October 19, 2017.}}</ref> Loeb's incorrect predictions that celestial objects are alien spaceships, his relationship with what ''[[Jalopnik]]'' describes as "nutty characters", and his interventions into areas of physics outside his background or work, have resulted in his increasing isolation from the scientific community.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Debord |first1=Matthew |title=Controversial Scientist Avi Loeb Is Lashing Out At NASA And Other Researchers As 3I/ATLAS Zooms Through Solar System |url=https://www.jalopnik.com/2034753/controversial-scientist-avi-loeb-lashing-out-nasa-researchers/ |access-date=June 16, 2026 |work=[[Jalopnik]] |date=November 28, 2025}}</ref><ref name="Ethan"/>

According to the ''[[Chicago Tribune]]'', Loeb's scientific peers consider him "outlandish and disingenuous, prone to sensational claims, more interested in being a celebrity than an astrophysicist — not to mention distracting and misleading".<ref name="Ct1">{{cite news |last1=Borrelli |first1=Christopher |title=The future of the search for alien life is with Harvard's Avi Loeb. He has plenty of critics. |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2024/01/08/the-future-of-the-search-for-alien-life-is-with-harvards-avi-loeb-he-has-plenty-of-critics/ |access-date=June 16, 2026 |work=[[Chicago Tribune]] |date=January 8, 2024}}</ref> During an appearance at the Humanities Festival, moderator [[Dan Hooper]] responded to a comment by Loeb on the [[Large Hadron Collider]] by stating "one of us on this stage is a particle physicist and it’s not you".<ref name="Ct1"/>

As of 2023, according to the ''[[New York Times]]'', some scientists were refusing to work with Loeb due to their contention he engaged in "ridiculous sensationalism".<ref name="NYT-20230724"/> Writing in [[Big Think]], [[Ethan Siegel]] credited Loeb's "outrageous and unsupportable claims" with helping draw attention to planetary science, despite what Siegel described as Loeb's own lack of expertise in the field.<ref name="Ethan">{{cite news |last1=Siegel |first1=Ethan |title=The humiliating truth behind Harvard astronomer's "alien" spherules |url=https://bigthink.com/starts-with-a-bang/truth-harvard-astronomer-alien-spherules/ |access-date=June 16, 2026 |work=[[Big Think]] |date=March 13, 2024}}</ref>

===Judaism and extraterrestrials===
{{further|Exotheology#Judaism}}
According to Loeb, the "fundamental question" is if the [[Ark of Covenant]] was a device used to communicate with extraterrestrials and if the Jewish people were chosen by a race of aliens and imbued with "information from beyond our planet".<ref>{{cite news |last1=Dworken |first1=Arye |title=The Chosen Seekers |url=https://www.tabletmag.com/sections/community/articles/chosen-seekers-jews-aliens-avi-loeb |access-date=June 16, 2026 |work=[[Tablet Magazine]] |date=June 15, 2026}}</ref> As reported by ''[[The Forward]]'', Loeb contends that Earth may not be safe for the Jewish people and leaving Earth could be advantageous due to the absence of [[antisemitism]] in outer space.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Irvy |first1=Benjamin |title=A comet is streaking across our solar system — is it an omen for Jews? |url=https://forward.com/culture/777277/31-atlas-interstellar-comet-extraterrestrial-jews-avi-loeb/ |access-date=June 16, 2026 |work=[[The Forward]] |date=October 21, 2025}}</ref> Writing on his [[Medium (website)|Medium]] blog, he has posited that "with long-term thinking, Jewish eschatology could be extended to trillions of years if a Jewish community with its synagogues and extraterrestrial Temple is established".<ref>{{cite web |last1=Loeb |first1=Avi |title=Extraterrestrial Intelligence and the Jews |url=https://avi-loeb.medium.com/extraterrestrial-intelligence-and-the-jews-9be04c7b6257 |website=avi-loeb.medium.com |publisher=[[Medium (website)|Medium]] |access-date=June 16, 2026}}</ref>

In 2024, Loeb delivered a speech in which he declared his view that the [[Messiah in Judaism|Messiah]] will be an alien who arrives from outer space.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wiedeman |first=Reeves |date=2024-02-12 |title=Bill Ackman Strikes Back |url=https://nymag.com/intelligencer/article/bill-ackman-war-harvard-mit-dei-claudine-gay.html |access-date=2024-02-23 |website=[[Intelligencer (website)|Intelligencer]] |language=en |quote=Loeb took the idea and suggested looking for hope from above. "My personal belief is that the Messiah will arrive, not necessarily from Brooklyn, as some Orthodox Jews believe, but rather from outer space," Loeb told the group.}}</ref> In 2025, Loeb was the speaker at "Extraterrestrial Intelligence and the Jews", an event presented by Lehrhaus.<ref>{{cite web |title=Extraterrestrial Intelligence and the Jews |url=https://www.lehr.haus/classes-old/extraterrestrial-intelligence-and-the-jews |website=lehr.haus |publisher=Lehrhaus |access-date=June 16, 2026}}</ref>

===UAP Science Advisory Council===
In June 2026, Loeb was named the chairperson of the newly formed UAP Science Advisory Council created at the request of the [[White House]]. The council will work in collaboration with federal agencies such as the [[Federal Bureau of Investigation]], the [[all-domain Anomaly Resolution Office]], and the [[Office of the Director for National Intelligence]], but will have no budget and no access to classified material.<ref name="apbinkley">{{Cite news| title= Harvard professor with polarizing alien theories is picked to lead new White House UFO council|author=Collin Binkley|work=Associated Press News|date=June 30, 2026|url=https://apnews.com/article/trump-ufo-council-avi-loeb-science-uaps-5798dd793b77aeb2d9baa99586ad8a85}}</ref>

The council's makeup, according to ''[[The Guardian]]'', was concerning to scientific observers since Loeb chose for its membership "apparently similar minds"<ref name="graunlusc"/> including "UFO activists"<ref name="apbinkley"/> and people who claimed the government was involved in a conspiracy to cover-up the existence of aliens.<ref name="graunlusc">{{cite news |last1=Luscombe |first1=Richard |title=The Harvard astronomer dubbed Trump's chief alien hunter starts by assuming UFOs human-made |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/jul/01/trump-alien-hunter-avi-loeb |access-date=July 3, 2026 |work=[[The Guardian]] |date=July 1, 2026}}</ref> Mainstream scientists such as [[Sean M. Kirkpatrick]] and [[Steve Desch]] were critical of the effort, with Desch asserting that Loeb's involvement cast doubt on its very legitimacy.<ref name="apbinkley"/>

===Interstellar: The Search for Extraterrestrial Life and Our Future in the Stars===
'''''Interstellar: The Search for Extraterrestrial Life and Our Future in the Stars''''' (also known as '''''Interstellar''''') is a [[popular science]] book written by American theoretical physicist and [[Harvard University]] astronomer Avi Loeb that was published by [[Mariner Books]] on 29 August 2023.<ref name="FN-20230814">{{cite news |last=Clark |first=-Jeffrey |title=Harvard physicist searching for UFO evidence says humanity will view alien intelligence like 'God' - 'A very advanced scientific civilization is a good approximation to God,' Prof. Loeb told Fox News Digital |url=https://www.foxnews.com/media/harvard-physicist-searching-ufo-evidence-says-humanity-will-view-alien-intelligence-like-god |date=14 August 2023 |work=[[Fox News]] |url-status=live |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20251022181423/https://www.foxnews.com/media/harvard-physicist-searching-ufo-evidence-says-humanity-will-view-alien-intelligence-like-god |archivedate=22 Oct 2025 }}</ref>

Sarah Scoles of ''[[Undark Magazine]]'' describes the book as a detailed account of "what a future expedition to find remnants of the first space rock, which hit the Earth in 2014, might look like." She catalogues the eclectic contents, noting that "In the span of two pages, for instance, Loeb moves from Plato’s Allegory of the Cave to the scientist who discovered the composition of stars to sunlight reflecting off the Moon to a solar telescope in Hawaii to the Parker Solar Probe in space to quantum tunneling (don’t ask) to Sisyphus and Albert Camus."<ref name="UM-20230901" />

Sarah Scoles of ''[[Undark Magazine]]'' states that "the book is a fairly disorganized, rambling affair whose topics and metaphors leap wildly to and fro", noting that while "There’s value in thought experiments, what-ifs, and shaking up academic conformity when it’s not adequately backed by data. But current scientific understanding doesn’t support the base of Loeb’s ideological pyramid."<ref name="UM-20230901">{{cite news |last=Scoles |first=Sarah |title=Book Review: One Man's Hunt for Alien Artifacts - In "Interstellar," Harvard professor Avi Loeb argues that searching for alien technology on Earth may save our species.|url=https://undark.org/2023/09/01/book-review-one-mans-hunt-for-alien-artifacts/ |date=1 September 2023 |work=[[Undark Magazine]] |url-status=live |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260218060524/https://undark.org/2023/09/01/book-review-one-mans-hunt-for-alien-artifacts/ |archivedate=18 Feb 2026 |accessdate=1 September 2023 }}</ref> Freelance writer Patrick Rapa, writing in ''[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]'', enjoyed the work, though he acknowledges that "Loeb’s peers are not on board. They call for caution and calm."<ref name="TPI-20230901">{{cite news |last=Rapa |first=Patrick |title=The 11 best books to read in September - We can't put down these tales of aliens, creeps, frauds, and villains. |url=https://www.inquirer.com/arts/books/11-best-books-read-september-20230901.html |date=1 September 2023 |work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]] |url-status=live |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20251111043751/https://www.inquirer.com/arts/books/11-best-books-read-september-20230901.html |archivedate= 11 Nov 2025 |accessdate=1 September 2023 }}</ref>

== Media appearances ==

In 2006, Loeb was featured in a ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]'' magazine cover story on the first stars, and in a ''[[Scientific American]]'' article on the Dark Ages of the universe. In 2008, he was featured in a [[Smithsonian magazine|''Smithsonian'']] magazine cover story on black holes, and in two ''[[Astronomy (magazine)|Astronomy]]'' magazine cover stories, one on the collision between the Milky Way and the Andromeda Galaxy and the second on the future state of our universe. In 2009, Loeb reviewed in a ''Scientific American'' article a new technique for imaging black hole silhouettes. Loeb received considerable media attention<ref>{{cite news|last=Lemonick|first=Michael D.|date=November 10, 2011|title=Is There a City on Pluto? Before You Answer, Consider: We've Never Looked. Two Scientists Want to Change That|magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]]|url=http://content.time.com/time/health/article/0,8599,2098834,00.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210616222811/https://content.time.com/time/health/article/0,8599,2098834,00.html|archive-date=June 16, 2021}}</ref> after proposing in 2011 (with E.L. Turner) a new technique for detecting artificially-illuminated objects in the Solar System and beyond,<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Loeb|first1=Abraham|last2=Turner|first2=Edwin L.|title=Detection Technique for Artificially Illuminated Objects in the Outer Solar System and Beyond|journal=[[Astrobiology (journal)|Astrobiology]]|date=April 2012|volume=12|issue=4|pages=290–294|doi=10.1089/ast.2011.0758|pmid=22490065|pmc=3330268|arxiv = 1110.6181 |bibcode = 2012AsBio..12..290L }}</ref> and showing in 2012 (with I. Ginsburg) that planets may transit hypervelocity stars or get kicked to a fraction of the speed of light near the black hole at the center of the Milky Way.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Ginsburg|first1=Idan|last2=Loeb|first2=Abraham|last3=Wegner|first3=Gary A.|title=Hypervelocity planets and transits around hypervelocity stars|journal=[[Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society]]|date=June 11, 2012|volume=423|issue=1|pages=948–954|doi=10.1111/j.1365-2966.2012.20930.x|doi-access=free |arxiv = 1201.1446 |bibcode = 2012MNRAS.423..948G |s2cid=119193699}}</ref>

He has been profiled by media including [[Science (journal)|''Science'']] magazine,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Irion |first1=Robert |title=From Cosmic Dawn to Milkomeda, and Beyond |journal=Science |department=NewsFocus |date=12 April 2013 |volume=340 |issue=6129 |pages=136–137 |doi=10.1126/science.340.6129.136 |url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.340.6129.136 |url-access=registration}}</ref> [[Discover (magazine)|''Discover'']],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cfa.harvard.edu/~loeb/FL1.pdf |title=First |author=Steve Nadis |website=Cfa.harvard.edu |access-date=February 19, 2016}}</ref> and ''[[The New York Times]]''.<ref name="NYT-20141202">{{cite news |last=Dreifus |first=Claudia |author-link=Claudia Dreifus |title=Much-Discussed Views That Go Way Back – Avi Loeb Ponders the Early Universe, Nature and Life |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2014/12/02/science/avi-loeb-ponders-the-early-universe-nature-and-life.html |date=December 2, 2014 |work=The New York Times |access-date=December 3, 2014 }}</ref> He has been interviewed by [[Astronomy (magazine)|''Astronomy'']] magazine,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.astronomy.com/magazine/superstars-of-astronomy-podcast/2015/05/abraham-loeb-cosmic-origins-and-our-galaxys-fate |title=Abraham Loeb: From cosmic origins to our galaxy's fate |website=Astronomy.com |date=May 6, 2015 |access-date=February 19, 2016}}</ref> by [[Lex Fridman Podcast|Lex Fridman]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 14, 2021 |title=#154 – Avi Loeb: Aliens, Black Holes, and the Mystery of the Oumuamua |url=https://lexfridman.com/avi-loeb/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210124003221/https://lexfridman.com/avi-loeb/ |archive-date=January 24, 2021 |access-date=April 1, 2021 |website=Lex Fridman}}</ref> 
''[[Let's Get Haunted]]'',<ref>{{Citation |title= Interstellar Object 3I/ATLAS Feat. Dr. Avi Loeb | date=September 24, 2025 |url=https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/lets-get-haunted/id1457775338?i=1000728181470 |access-date=2025-10-02 |language=en}}</ref>
[[Joe Rogan Experience|Joe Rogan]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 16, 2021 |title=#1596 - Avi Loeb |url=https://open.spotify.com/episode/0y7Vfzeua0TyLSAq3CUktH |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210119154520/https://open.spotify.com/episode/0y7Vfzeua0TyLSAq3CUktH |archive-date=January 19, 2021 |access-date=April 1, 2021 |website=[[Spotify]]}}</ref> [[Mick West]],<ref>{{Citation |title=TFTRH #55: Avi Loeb and The Galileo Project | date=August 10, 2021 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VQqdgNG-rJg |access-date=2021-11-08 |language=en}}</ref> and by the ''[[H3 podcast|H3 Podcast]]''.<ref>{{Citation |title=Avi Loeb - Aliens, Black Holes & The End of the Universe - H3 Podcast #257 | date=November 4, 2022 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gyBnTFJo7PM |access-date=2022-11-04 |language=en}}</ref> On August 24, 2023, ''[[The New York Times]]'' published an article about Loeb and his search for signs of extraterrestrial life.<ref name="NYT-20230824">{{cite news |last=Fletcher |first=Seth |title=How a Harvard Professor Became the World's Leading Alien Hunter – Avi Loeb's single-minded search for extraterrestrial life has made him the most famous practicing astronomer in the country — and possibly the most controversial. + comment |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/08/24/magazine/avi-loeb-alien-hunter.html#permid=127237844 |date=August 24, 2023 |work=[[The New York Times]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20230824140851/https://www.nytimes.com/2023/08/24/magazine/avi-loeb-alien-hunter.html#permid=127237844 |archive-date=August 24, 2023 |access-date=August 24, 2023 }}</ref>
During an appearance on [[Joe Rogan]]'s [[The Joe Rogan Experience|podcast]], he also claimed that whether an ancient "sophisticated civilization" existed on Earth before humanity is a credible question to ask.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://avi-loeb.medium.com/are-uaps-relics-from-an-earlier-civilization-on-earth-86d1190c6539|title=Are UAPs Relics from an Earlier Civilization on Earth?|date=Nov 21, 2023|access-date=31 Jan 2026|website=avi-loeb.medium.com|last=Loeb|first=Avi|ref=avi-loeb.medium.com-Earlier Civilization}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://avi-loeb.medium.com/lost-civilizations-from-our-cosmic-past-a778e50b5c55|title=Lost Civilizations from Our Cosmic Past|date=Oct 13, 2022|access-date=31 Jan 2026|website=avi-loeb.medium.com|last=Loeb|first=Avi|ref=avi-loeb.medium.com-lost-civilizations}}</ref><ref name="singjupost.com-Rogan-Loeb-Transcript">{{cite web |title=Transcript: Physicist Avi Loeb on Joe Rogan Podcast #2401|url=https://singjupost.com/transcript-physicist-avi-loeb-on-joe-rogan-podcast-2401/|website=singjupost.com|access-date=31 January 2026|date=October 29, 2025}}</ref><ref name="scientificamerican.com-avi-loeb-not-kidding">{{cite web |last1=Billings|first1=Lee|title=Astronomer Avi Loeb Says Aliens Have Visited, and He's Not Kidding|url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/astronomer-avi-loeb-says-aliens-have-visited-and-hes-not-kidding1/|website=Scientific American|access-date=31 January 2026|language=en|date=1 April 2021}}</ref>

Loeb also regularly writes opinion essays on science and policy.<ref>{{cite book|asin=B014GCTXF0 |title=From the First Star to Milkomeda, Abraham Loeb, Dror Burstein, Todd Hasak-Lowy, Noa Moav |date=August 24, 2015 |publisher=Abraham Loeb }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cfa.harvard.edu/~loeb/Opinion.html |title=Opinion Essays by Abraham Loeb |website=cfa.harvard.edu~/loeb/Opinion.html|date=March 18, 2018 |access-date=March 18, 2018}}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==

Loeb has received many honors, including:<ref name="CV"/>
* 1987 – The Kennedy Prize of the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]]
* 2002 – [[Guggenheim Fellowship]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Avi Loeb |url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/avi-loeb/ |website=John Simon Guggenheim Foundation}}</ref>
* 2004 – Distinguished Visiting Professorship at the Faculty of Physics & Einstein Center for Theoretical Physics of the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]]
* 2006/7 – John Bahcall Lecturer at the [[Tel Aviv University]]
* 2006 – Salpeter Lectureship at [[Cornell University]]
* 2012 – ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]'' magazine's 25 most influential people in space.<ref>{{cite web |author1=David Bjerklie |title=The 25 Most Influential People in Space |url=https://www.cfa.harvard.edu/~loeb/TIME.pdf |access-date=February 19, 2016 |website=cfa.harvard.edu}}</ref>
* 2012 – Elected member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]
* 2012 – Galileo Galilei Chair (Cattedra Galileiana) Award of the [[Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa|Scuola Normale Superiore]], [[Pisa, Italy]]
* 2013 – [[Chambliss Astronomical Writing Award]] from the [[American Astronomical Society]], for ''How Did the First Stars and Galaxies Form?'' (2010)
* 2014 – Member of the Board on Physics and Astronomy (BPA) of the [[National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine]]
* 2015 – Elected Fellow of the [[International Academy of Astronautics]] (IAA) SETI Permanent Committee
* 2015 – Elected Member of the [[American Physical Society]] (APS)
* 2020 – Appointed to the [[President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology]]<ref>{{cite web |title=PCAST_Members |url=https://science.osti.gov/About/PCAST/About/Members |access-date=July 1, 2020 |website=osti.gov}}</ref>
